motion.name: ease-standard

motion.name: dur-standard
motion.purpose: State changes only: hover, focus, the ruler flag, the arrow slide.

motion.name: dur-route-draw
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the route map's corridors draw themselves on entry.

motion.name: dur-reduced
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: --dur becomes 0ms, scroll-behavior becomes auto, the route draw is shown already drawn.

motion.name: dur-board-flip
motion.purpose: The decision board flips as the reader re-filters: a two-frame rotateX on every visible row, triggered by the reader's own control and never on page entry.

narrative.overview:
The world is an international airport sign system: an overhead band you read at a distance, a gantry of section signs, a white sheet of rules, and an arrow that tells you where to go next. Nothing in this system is a card, a panel with a soft edge, or a floating object. Every edge is a drawn rule — 3px black where a band begins or ends, 1px hairlines inside a table, 2px where a figure's axis is.

The personality is blunt, engineered, unhurried. The whole visual argument rests on a single saturated yellow that is spent only on things that point — the masthead band, the section gantry and its current-section inversion, the section opener bands, the destination gate on the decision board, the peak hour in the demand curve, the peak day, the peak month, the top-ranked locality, and the break-even flag on the price scale. Everything else is black type on white over a warm paper ground.

Two voices do all the work. Public Sans, a humanist sans, carries prose, band messages and the monumental numbers. Roboto Mono carries everything that is a fact: parameters, numerals in tables, unit conventions, ward and cluster codes, source ids, axis labels, ticks and captions.
keyCharacteristics: One yellow, one meaning: wayfinding. It never sits behind body text and never fills a page.
Flat by construction. box-shadow appears once in the whole codebase, as none.
Depth is drawn, not cast: borders, rules, inverted bands, tonal grounds.
Two type voices with a hard job split: Public Sans for words, Roboto Mono for facts.
A 68-character reading measure that never yields to a figure or a table.
The arrow is the memorable moment: one black triangle, re-pointed whenever a filter changes.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: --signal is reserved for wayfinding and for nothing else: the masthead band, the section openers, the gantry's current section, the gate the arrow points at, the one hour, day, month or locality the demand data says to go to, and the break-even flag. If a new surface wants yellow for emphasis on something that is not a destination, it does not get yellow.

rules.name: The Ink Stays Ink Rule
rules.body: On a yellow ground the text is --signal-ink (black), never a tint of the yellow and never a grey. The one exception is deliberate and local: .gate--target .gate__v and .gate__v i drop to rgba(17,17,17,0.72) because those are secondary labels inside a yellow row.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: The reading surface is --paper. --ground is the world outside the sheet and --panel is the world inside a component that is inert. Nothing else is a background.

rules.name: The Fact Is Monospaced Rule
rules.body: If a string is a number, a code, a unit, an id or a parameter, it is set in Roboto Mono with tabular numerals. Prose is Public Sans. The exception is the monumental figure in the key result panel, which is a headline and speaks in the display voice, carrying a 14x14px yellow flag square as its only ornament.

rules.name: The Monospace Is Not Costume Rule
rules.body: Mono is used for measurement and data, never as a technical texture. There is no monospaced label where a word would do better.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If a surface needs to separate itself from another, it is separated by a rule, a rule weight, or a tonal step — never by a shadow.

rules.name: The One Move Rule
rules.body: One three-dimensional gesture exists in this system: the corridor button's resting four-degree perspective tilt, which flattens and lifts two pixels on hover and focus. Do not add a second. If a new surface wants depth, it gets a border.

dos: Do spend --signal only on something that points: a band, a gate, a peak, a flag, a target.
Do set any number, code, unit, id or parameter in Roboto Mono, with tabular-nums.
Do separate surfaces with a drawn rule — 3px --rule for structure, 1px --rule-soft inside, 1px --rule-hair between table rows.
Do keep prose inside --measure: 68ch and let .result, .chart, .tbl-scroll, figure, .board, .flow, .routemap, .zonebtn, .doc__grid and .verdict break out of it.
Do paint a scale's colour from the same values that place its ticks, so the two can never disagree.
Do give every figure a role="img" and a written label, and every wide table a keyboard-reachable role="region" wrapper.
Do give every interactive element a visible :focus-visible outline (2px --ink, 2px offset).
Do use --ink-3 (5.4:1) as the floor for small text and --ink-2 (11.4:1) for running prose.
Do keep the two zone series distinguishable by weight and hatch so every figure survives greyscale print.
donts: Don't put yellow behind running text, use it as a page background, or spend it on emphasis that is not wayfinding.
Don't add a shadow. The system has none, and every separation is already a rule.
Don't round a corner. The only radius in the system is 0.
Don't use a glyph, an emoji or an icon font for the arrow, the pictogram or the chevron. They are drawn: CSS triangles, black squares, gradient chevrons.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading. The heading carries its own weight.
Don't turn a citation into a highlighted chip. .cite is a plain mono superscript.
Don't colour two data series by hue. Use weight and hatch.
Don't invent a second three-dimensional move.
Don't scroll a wide table off the edge of the sheet at desktop widths, or cut it off on a phone — wrap it in .tbl-scroll and let it scroll.
Don't print the gantry, or let a yellow band lose its colour in print.
Don't launder a caveat into a footnote.
